intended_object: The R-algebra homomorphism R[x_0,…,x_n]/I_n → R[a,b] induced by the monomial parametrization x_i ↦ a^{n-i} b^i of the rational normal curve. Here I_n is the ideal generated by the 2×2 minors of the Hankel matrix. This is the map whose injectivity identifies the Hankel ideal with the toric ideal. Inferred from the docstring and the module.
explanation:
`Source R n` is `MvPolynomial (Fin (n+1)) R` and `Target R` is `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R`. The underlying map `AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom R R (rncExponent n)` sends a monomial x^α to a^{Σ α_i (n-i)} b^{Σ α_i i}. In particular it sends x_i to a^{n-i} b^i, which is the standard parametrization of the rational normal curve. `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ` descends this map to the quotient by the Hankel ideal (the span of the Hankel minors). The proof that it does so is `hankelIdeal_le_ker`. So this is the canonical induced map from the quotient to R[a,b], as the docstring says.

It is stated for an arbitrary commutative ring R. That is the natural generality, because quotients by ideals need a ring. Mathlib has no specialized counterpart; the definition just combines the general Mathlib constructions `mapDomainAlgHom` and `Quotient.liftₐ`.
